changes.historical_text: Select 1 monster on your side of the field and send it to the Graveyard. Increase your Life Points by an amount equal to the original ATK of the monster.
changes.modern_text: Select 1 monster on your side of the field and send it to the Graveyard. Increase your Life Points by an amount equal to the original ATK of the monster.
changes.summary: Era cost eligibility, not a text erratum: the GOAT script's cost filter is `c:IsAbleToGraveAsCost() or c:IsType(TYPE_TOKEN)`, so a Token may be sent for the cost (its ATK is forced to 0, `local atk=(tc:IsType(TYPE_TOKEN) and 0) or tc:GetTextAttack()`, so the resolution recovers 0 LP), while the modern script filters on `Card.IsAbleToGraveAsCost` alone and refuses Tokens, making the card unactivatable when your field holds only Tokens. The cdb text of the GOAT entry and the modern cdb text are identical; the difference lives only in the script. Chronology is unresolved: the card has no Yugipedia Card Errata page and the packet carries no dated source for when Token cost eligibility changed.

review.notes: No Yugipedia Card Errata page for this card (packet `errata_page.missing: true`), so there is no English text lineage; literal texts are copied from the packet's GOAT implementation `text` and `modern_text` fields, which are byte-identical - the record carries no period display text and no set-release dating is possible. Verified against the on-disk scripts (goat/c504700180.lua vs official/c21070956.lua): the only substantive delta is the added `s.cfilter` Token clause and the Token-ATK-as-0 branch; activation timing, EVENT_FREE_CHAIN, and the LP-recovery resolution are unchanged. Considered `engine`: data/rule-profiles/tcg-goat.json (DUEL_MODE_GOAT expansion) carries no flag governing Token eligibility as a send-to-Graveyard cost, so the per-card script is the only carrier and this is not a redundant duplicate of a rule-profile flag. The card does not appear on EdisonFormat.com's functional-errata list, so no community corroboration is available. Chronology deliberately left unresolved rather than guessed.
